D.t: Dan Ahlers trails by 13.0 and wins 5% of simulations. Closing it takes about 25,065 voters switching sides, or 50,130 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +22.1 and R +3.4. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The polls page average is R +18.0. Your best recent poll is Concord Public Opinion Partners (D) at R +12.7; your worst is Mason-Dixon for South Dakota News Watch and USD Chiesman Center at R +19.2. 3 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Minnehaha, a projected net 8,329 votes; Oglala Lakota, a projected net 2,774 votes; Clay, a projected net 1,680 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Minnehaha, D +10.0, 21.7% of the vote; Pennington, R +9.4, 13.1% of the vote; Lincoln, R +8.0, 8.2% of the vote; Brown, R +8.8, 4.0% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Dan Ahlers runs furthest behind in Butte, Hughes, Meade. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 88% of voters, 42 to 57, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.42 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 72% of voters, 41 to 57, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.62 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 61% of voters, 49 to 49, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.04 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Dan Ahlers: Immigration voters 20 to 78, Voters who can afford daily costs 39 to 58, Small counties 41 to 58. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
